task_1.title: Avoid requiring cloudpickle on PyPy for test extras
task_1.description: The update narrows the optional cloudpickle dependency so it is only required on CPython, preventing PyPy environments from pulling in an unsupported package when installing the test-related extras.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that installing the library's test-related optional dependencies does not require cloudpickle on PyPy, while preserving cloudpickle availability on CPython where that compatibility path is supported.

expectation.grounded: The optional dependency set used for test-oriented installation should declare cloudpickle only for the CPython implementation. On PyPy, installation of that extra should no longer require or resolve cloudpickle. On CPython, cloudpickle should remain part of the extra so the existing cloudpickle compatibility path stays available.
expectation.conceptual: Optional test dependencies should adapt to the active Python implementation. Users on PyPy should be able to install the package's test extras without encountering an unsupported cloudpickle dependency, and users on CPython should continue to receive the cloudpickle-related compatibility support.

constraints.grounded: Do not broaden this change into a general runtime dependency update or alter unrelated extras. Preserve cloudpickle as part of the relevant optional dependency group for CPython, and avoid introducing a requirement that PyPy import or install cloudpickle through that extra.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the fix limited to implementation-specific optional dependency resolution. Existing supported behavior on CPython should continue unchanged, and environments that do not support cloudpickle should not be forced into that dependency.

behavior: Installing the test-related optional dependencies on CPython includes cloudpickle.
Installing the same optional dependencies on PyPy excludes cloudpickle.
The package no longer treats cloudpickle as a universally required dependency for that optional extra across all Python implementations.
This change affects environment-specific dependency resolution rather than the library's production runtime API.
acceptance_criteria: When a user installs the package's relevant test extra on CPython, cloudpickle should be included as an optional dependency.
When a user installs the same extra on PyPy, cloudpickle should not be required or selected.
When using the library in normal production installation without that extra, this update should not add any new runtime dependency requirements.
The implementation-specific dependency behavior should distinguish CPython from PyPy without changing unrelated optional dependency groups.

task_2.title: Fix coverage reporting for attrs-generated repr methods
task_2.description: Upgrading from attrs 21.3.0 to 21.4.0 fixes a regression where projects using attrs could cause `coverage report` to fail when no `--source` filter is configured. The change makes dynamically generated repr functions identify themselves with unique synthetic filenames so coverage and similar tooling no longer treat multiple generated repr bodies as the same source artifact.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to attrs 21.4.0 restores successful coverage reporting for projects that use attrs-generated representations, especially when running coverage without specifying `--source`.

expectation.grounded: Attrs-generated `__repr__` implementations should no longer share one generic synthetic filename. In 21.4.0, repr code produced by attrs must carry a unique generated filename per class context so tools such as `coverage report` can process imports and executed code without failing when attrs is present and coverage is run without `--source`.
expectation.conceptual: Using attrs should not break coverage reporting. Generated repr methods must appear as distinct generated code artifacts so reporting tools can complete normally instead of failing because unrelated generated repr code is conflated.

constraints.grounded: The fix is limited to the generated repr code identity used by attrs internals. Existing repr behavior, repr output semantics, and normal attrs class usage must remain unchanged apart from eliminating coverage-report failures caused by non-unique generated filenames.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should resolve the reporting regression without changing what reprs do for users or introducing new requirements for how projects configure coverage.

behavior: Attrs-generated `__repr__` functions use unique synthetic filenames instead of a shared generic repr filename.
Projects that import or use attrs and are executed under coverage can run `coverage report` successfully even when no `--source` option is provided.
Tooling that distinguishes executed code by code-object filename no longer conflates multiple attrs-generated repr implementations into one synthetic source location.
acceptance_criteria: When a project uses attrs and is run with coverage without specifying `--source`, generating a coverage report should complete without an error caused by attrs-generated repr code.
When multiple attrs classes rely on generated repr methods, their generated code should be distinguishable by unique synthetic filenames rather than one shared filename.
When upgrading from 21.3.0 to 21.4.0, user-visible repr behavior should remain the same except that coverage reporting no longer regresses.
